Summary

The true story of one girl's escape from the wilds of the counter-culture movement. In the late 1960s, Cea Sunrise Person's family left their suburban hippie existence in California to live off the grid in Canada's idyllic wilderness. Led by Cea's eccentric grandfather, they called a canvas teepee home, grew pot, and hunted and gathered to survive, weathering fierce storms and food shortages.

North of Normal is a 2022 Canadian drama film, directed by Carly Stone . [ 2 ] Based on the 2014 memoir of the same name by Cea Sunrise Person , the film centres on her unconventional childhood living in the wilderness as the daughter of a hippie mother. [ 3 ]
The film's cast includes Sarah Gadon , Amanda Fix , Robert Carlyle , River Price-Maenpaa, James D'Arcy and Benedict Samuel .
The film was shot in 2021 in Northern Ontario , primarily in and around Sudbury , North Bay and Mattawa . [ 3 ]

North of Normal

Audiobook
 Listen to a sample Listen to a sample
Sex, drugs, and . . . bug stew? In the vein of The Glass Castle and Wild, Cea Sunrise Person's compelling memoir of a childhood spent with her dysfunctional counter-culture family in the Canadian wilderness—a searing story of physical, emotional, and psychological survival.
In the late 1960s, riding the crest of the counterculture movement, Cea's family left a comfortable existence in

...

For Michelle, however, now long separated from Cea's father, there was one crucial element missing: a man. When Cea was five, Michelle took her on the road with a new boyfriend. As the trio set upon a series of ill-fated adventures, Cea began to question both her highly unusual world and the hedonistic woman at the centre of it

...

photos, North of Normal is Cea's funny, shocking, heartbreaking, and triumphant tale of self-discovery and acceptance, adversity, and strength that will leave no listener unmoved.
